description: Snail is a poet snail. Or rather, a snail poet. They were born in a metal bin by a library, cushioned by tossed away sheets of Virginia Woolf’s Orlando. They have ventured far and wide in order to be here, in this garden. Noah, a university dropout, is pretty annoyed by the whole thing. While Noah tries to rebuild their parents’ garden (and their own life), Snail won’t stop waxing poetic about tomato plants and the fluidity of gender. Will this unlikely duo become friends, or is it true that snails are solitary creatures?

A Canada and Halifax Fringe premiere, The Trouble with My Hair examines gender, sexual, and racial identity through Cheng’s evolving relationship with her hair—and the stylists who helped shape it. With humor, vulnerability, and sharp cultural insight, Cheng reveals how something as simple as hair can carry the weight of family expectations, beauty standards, queerness, and personal agency. Blending theatrical storytelling with narrative art, this performance invites audiences into a deeply personal yet universally resonant journey of self-discovery and self-love.
credits: Developed with and Directed by Jessica Lynn Johnson

description: The Ward and The Watershed takes place in a prison, on an island, in an ocean, on a planet, not so different from our own. This prison is built around a spring of fresh water which is controlled by The Warden. The Warden hoards all the water for himself and uses it to control the guards. The story follows an argument between Deo (active) and Chuck (passive) about whether or not it is worth it to try. Chuck has settled and believes he has found balance in his own life within the prison. Deo challenges Chuck’s beliefs and is set in unraveling them.

White Samosa is a spicy stand-up special from Vancouver’s first multilingual comedian, Harmeet Singh Kohli. Armed with accents and unapologetic punchlines, Harmeet takes aim at cultural appropriation, Uber-driving stereotypes, and everything in between.

Imagine a convention or conference where all the speakers have gotten sick and random audience members have to step up, improvising their way through each slide. That a good indication of what you’ll experience at Nerd Nite Halifax’s Whose Presentation Is It Anyway? Six smart and talented individuals will arrive to present on topics that may range from video games and romance novels to marine biology and rocket science. We’ll then shuffle the decks and each contestant will present slides from someone else that they have never seen before. The winner will be chosen by the audience.
